source_snapshot.procedure: Verify SUT recipe, clear logs, execute TBD during-test procedure, collect results/photos and inspect new logs.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek identifies the vendor MODS dependency but provides only a truncated insecure help query and defers the actual module; it supplies no CPU scope, DVFS stimulus, evidence or acceptance rule.

original_test_intent.purpose: Execute the vendor-approved MODS CPUDVFS test for the exact SUT to exercise and evaluate CPU dynamic voltage/frequency behavior under the platform recipe, then inspect the complete tool result and newly generated platform logs.
original_test_intent.target: The exact CPU package, cores or frequency-policy domains selected by the owner-supplied MODS CPUDVFS recipe on the verified SUT; the source does not identify CPU vendor, architecture or domain mapping.
original_test_intent.scope: Recipe/configuration verification, an owner-defined CPUDVFS module run, collection of results/photos and delta inspection of dmesg, syslog and SEL within the source's 10-minute attended and 10-minute machine-time estimates. It is not a `mods -h` check or a generic CPU stress substitute.
original_test_intent.operation: Preserve a traceable pre-test log baseline, validate the exact vendor package/module/recipe and CPU mapping, run the bounded CPUDVFS workflow with recipe-required telemetry and stop controls, capture every result, inspect post-test log deltas and restore any authorized test-only state.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: The workbook estimates 10 attended and 10 machine minutes but the active test duration, transition sequence, load pattern and repetitions are TBD. Use only the supplied recipe values and do not infer them from the estimates.
original_test_intent.expected_result: No PASS definition exists in the source. Completion requires the exact supplied module to finish with complete evidence and safe restoration; PASS additionally requires all vendor/platform CPUDVFS result rules and log/health criteria supplied by the owner to be met.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: SUT/CPU/firmware/OS identity and CPU-domain map; MODS build/hash and exact recipe; approved limits and acceptance rules; preserved pre-clear log export or owner-approved timestamp baseline; exact launch and full stdout/stderr/status; recipe-defined frequency/voltage/load/thermal/power evidence; module subresults; post-test log delta; restoration and final health.
ambiguities: The During Test procedure and Criteria are both TBD.
The exact MODS build, CPUDVFS module, CPU target/domain mapping, transition/load pattern, limits, duration and iterations are absent.
The source requests log clearing but does not define export, authorization, clear mechanism or whether timestamp-based delta evidence is acceptable.
The owner-defined relationship between MODS results, measured DVFS behavior and PASS is absent.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly treats the vendor package/recipe gap as readiness rather than permanent BLOCKED and refuses to invent a CPUDVFS command or PASS rule. However, its proposed precheck still disables SSH host-key verification, and its blanket ban on log clearing does not preserve the source's explicit clean-log intent or provide a controlled alternative.

applicable_history.decision: V2 establishes the valid REQUIRES boundary and high-risk load controls, but no later user ruling supplies the missing MODS CPUDVFS recipe or resolves the source log-clear step.
Destructive or state-changing preparation requires explicit authorization and evidence preservation; a test must not claim PASS while its criteria remain undefined.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Keep the REQUIRES class. Require the proprietary module/recipe and explicit CPU-domain mapping, preserve the 10-minute estimates without inventing active duration, replace insecure SSH, and reconcile the source's log-clear step through pre-export plus approval or an owner-approved timestamp baseline.

available_now: The source identifies a MODS CPUDVFS vendor-module intent, pre/post log workflow and 10-minute attended/machine estimates.
Read-only SUT/CPU/topology, firmware/OS, package-presence, current policy/telemetry and log baselines can be collected before execution approval.
missing_inputs: The vendor/platform owner must supply the controlled MODS build, integrity reference, exact CPUDVFS module/command/configuration, supported CPU-domain mapping and stack prerequisites.
The CPU/SI owner must supply transition/load sequence, duration/iterations, frequency/voltage/thermal/power limits, expected module results, permitted throttling and log/health acceptance rules.
The lab owner must decide and authorize the pre-test log-baseline method, maintenance window, live monitoring, emergency stop and recovery.
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The vendor/platform owner supplies the package and recipe; the CPU/SI owner supplies target mapping and acceptance/stop rules; the lab/system owner supplies authorization, monitoring and recovery including log handling.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Record SUT, CPU packages/cores/policy domains, BIOS/firmware, OS/kernel, current frequency/governor/telemetry through platform-supported interfaces, BMC health and existing dmesg/syslog/SEL without clearing them.
Verify the package file/version/hash and inspect complete supported help or manifest data locally or through authenticated host-key-verified access without launching CPUDVFS.
prohibited_until_closed: Do not invent a MODS command, map the wrong CPU/domain, treat help output as execution, infer voltage directly when the recipe does not expose it, clear logs without export and approval, disable host-key verification, expose credentials, apply an unapproved load/state change, or declare PASS while criteria are TBD.
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: Approve the exact package/recipe/target map and quantitative rules; export and hash baseline logs before any authorized clear or use an approved timestamp marker; prove monitoring/storage/recovery; run once under supervision; reconcile every module result and log delta; restore state and obtain owner disposition.

revision_candidate.test_name: Vendor MODS CPU DVFS Functional Test
revision_candidate.purpose: Execute the approved MODS CPUDVFS recipe on the intended CPU domains and evaluate the tool, DVFS, health and log evidence against owner-supplied criteria.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The exact owner-identified CPU server platform, BIOS/firmware, OS/kernel/driver stack and controlled MODS build supported by the CPUDVFS recipe; do not infer Intel, AMD or Arm semantics without that recipe.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Every CPU package/core or frequency-policy domain explicitly named by the recipe, one bounded run using recipe-defined transitions, load, duration and iterations. Preserve the source's 10-minute attended/machine estimates as planning data only.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Verified SUT/CPU/domain map; BIOS/firmware/OS; approved MODS package/hash/module/configuration; exact command; supported prerequisites; DVFS transition/load/duration/iteration definition; measurable limits and PASS/FAIL rules; log-baseline policy; secure access; monitoring/storage; authorization; stop and recovery procedure.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Capture immutable identity, CPU-domain/current-state and health evidence. Export and hash dmesg/syslog/SEL before an explicitly authorized clear, or record an owner-approved timestamp baseline without clearing. Validate the package/recipe and launch only the supplied bounded CPUDVFS module. Capture complete output and recipe-defined telemetry, enforce stops, inspect post-test log deltas and restore every authorized test-only setting.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Correct SUT and CPU-domain mapping verified; package/recipe/criteria compatible and approved; no competing workload; authenticated host-key-verified access; time sync, storage, console, BMC and live monitoring ready; baseline logs preserved; maintenance and recovery authorized.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Identity/topology/domain map; firmware/OS and package/hash/configuration; signed recipe/criteria; pre-test state and exported log baseline/clear audit or timestamp marker; exact launch; full stdout/stderr/status/subresults/timestamps; recipe-defined DVFS/load/thermal/power evidence; dmesg/syslog/SEL deltas; stop/recovery events; restored CPU policy and final health.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The owner-approved MODS CPUDVFS recipe and result/limit rules for the exact platform. Because source Criteria are TBD, no vendor PASS, exit code, observed transition or clean log may be treated as sufficient until those rules are supplied.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Dedicated approved SUT. Do not guess commands, CPU mappings, voltage/frequency limits or result semantics; clear logs without preserved export and approval; bypass SSH trust; hide output; continue after telemetry loss or safety fault; alter firmware/DVFS tables outside the recipe; or automatically rerun an unexplained failure.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Explicit approval is required for package installation, the CPUDVFS load and state changes, any log clearing, supplied limits, maintenance window and recovery. Read-only preparation alone does not authorize execution.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Automation may collect inventory, execute the supplied recipe, supervise stops and assemble evidence. Vendor/CPU engineers define module semantics and acceptance; the lab owner authorizes log handling and load and performs out-of-band recovery if needed.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Stop the controlled module, preserve complete partial output and current logs/state, restore only recipe-authorized CPU settings, verify all CPUs and services healthy and use approved console/OOB recovery if unresponsive. Do not rerun until the owner resolves and reauthorizes the event.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Wrong SUT/CPU/domain/package/recipe; absent criteria or approval; insecure access; failed baseline preservation; monitoring/output/time-sync/storage loss; temperature/power/frequency/voltage or throttling outside approved limits; hang/crash/reset; new machine-check/RAS/kernel/BMC error; unexpected state change; module anomaly; or failed restoration.

identified_defects: The source's executable procedure and criteria are TBD, so no command or PASS rule can be inferred.
DeepSeek's truncated help command does not execute CPUDVFS and uses plaintext-password and host-key-bypass patterns.
V2 removes plaintext-password use but still proposes `StrictHostKeyChecking=no`, contradicting its secure-access requirement.
V2 forbids log clearing without explicitly preserving the source's requested clean-log intent through authorized pre-export or timestamp-delta handling.
V2 does not preserve the 10-minute source estimates or require an exact CPU package/core/policy-domain target map.
reason_for_change: Prevent an undefined proprietary DVFS workflow from being replaced by a help query or generic stress run, while handling the source's destructive log-clear step transparently and removing V2's insecure SSH example.

new_technical_evidence.title: Source testcase Wistron-HW-00479-V002
new_technical_evidence.supports: The source identifies a MODS CPUDVFS test, explicitly requests pre-test log clearing and post-test log review, budgets 10/10 minutes, and leaves both During Test and Criteria TBD.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: A search of public NVIDIA documentation on 2026-10-13 found no applicable official definition of this server CPUDVFS module; vendor-controlled recipe semantics remain required.

removed_ambiguities: Separates the 10-minute planning estimates from unknown active duration and iterations.
Requires the recipe to identify actual CPU packages/cores/policy domains rather than assuming architecture or index coverage.
Defines evidence-preserving options for the source log-clear request instead of silently deleting or ignoring it.
Makes complete module evidence and supplied criteria—not help output or exit code alone—the completion boundary.
resolved_blockers: The absent package and recipe remain provider-closable readiness gaps, not proof of permanent automation impossibility.
Read-only inventory and baseline preservation can proceed before module execution.
remaining_blockers: Execution and verdict await the controlled MODS build, exact CPUDVFS recipe/target mapping, quantitative acceptance/stop rules, approved log-baseline method, authorization and recovery.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 retains V2's correct classification but eliminates its host-key-bypass command, preserves rather than silently contradicts the source log-clear intent, and makes timing, CPU-domain coverage and undefined PASS semantics auditable.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The validator recovered the exact recipe-defined CPU-domain scope, bounded run, 10-minute planning-only meaning, preserved or timestamped log baseline, secure access, complete telemetry/log evidence, restoration and no automatic rerun. It rejected vendor-name-as-command, guessed mappings/limits and exit-code-only completion. Criteria TBD is TEST_CASE_DOCUMENT_DEFECT; missing recipe/platform data are PLATFORM_HANDOFF_DEFECT. Its statement that execution is currently blocked describes readiness, not an automation-classification change.
